nodes.label: APT42 / CALANQUE ION
nodes.notes: Iranian cyber-espionage actor focused on information collection and surveillance. First-party threat intelligence records activity from 2015 and a last-observed date of 2026-08-11. Attribution is assessed, not a claim that every overlapping vendor cluster is identical. Sources: Google Cloud 2022 and 2024 APT42 reporting; Google TAG 2024; current multi-source threat-intelligence records.

nodes.label: Alias / overlap set
nodes.notes: Frequently reported overlaps include Charming Kitten, TA453, Mint Sandstorm, Phosphorus, Cobalt Illusion, ITG18, UNC788 and CALANQUE. Vendor scopes differ; treat these as naming overlaps unless a source explicitly equates the clusters.

nodes.label: IRGC-IO nexus
nodes.notes: Mandiant assesses APT42 operates on behalf of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Intelligence Organization. Google TAG describes APT42 as associated with the IRGC. Confidence: High, based on independent first-party reporting; precise organizational control remains an intelligence assessment.

nodes.label: Evidence snapshot • 01 Sep 2026
nodes.notes: Analytical visualization, not an IOC feed. Solid links denote well-supported relationships; dashed links denote observed operational flow; dotted links denote assessed overlap or contextual relevance. Key sources: cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/apt42-charms-cons-compromises; cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/untangling-iran-apt42-operations; blog.google/threat-analysis-group/iranian-backed-group-steps-up-phishing-campaigns-against-israel-us; blog.checkpoint.com/security/educated-manticore-reemerges-iranian-spear-phishing-campaign-targeting-high-profile-figures.

nodes.label: Recon + persona design
nodes.notes: Open-source research identifies high-value individuals, personal email addresses and relevant professional interests. AI-assisted drafting has been observed, but lure quality alone is not attribution.

nodes.label: Journalist / expert persona
nodes.notes: APT42 has impersonated journalists, researchers, event organizers, think-tank staff and cybersecurity professionals to establish credibility. ATT&CK: T1656 Impersonation.

nodes.label: Trust-building contact
nodes.notes: The actor commonly sustains benign correspondence before moving the target to another channel or introducing a lure. This long-con social-engineering pattern is central to the actor's tradecraft.

nodes.label: Credential spearphishing
nodes.notes: Observed delivery includes direct links, links in otherwise benign PDFs, and links sent through messaging services after rapport-building.

nodes.label: Hosted lure / redirect
nodes.notes: APT42 abuses legitimate cloud services, URL shorteners and attacker-controlled lookalike domains to host or redirect victims to credential-harvesting pages.

nodes.label: Credential + MFA capture
nodes.notes: Phishing kits have captured passwords, authentication codes, device PINs and recovery codes. Phishing-resistant hardware keys materially reduce this path.

nodes.label: Valid account access
nodes.notes: Stolen credentials and authentication material are used to access personal or corporate email and cloud services.

nodes.label: Mailbox / cloud account
nodes.notes: Personal accounts can be attractive because they may have weaker protections than managed corporate identities.

nodes.label: Email + cloud collection
nodes.notes: Observed objectives include email, contacts, calendars, cloud files and other strategically relevant account data.

nodes.label: Strategic data exfiltration
nodes.notes: Reporting describes mailbox synchronization, cloud exports and covert collection of documents relevant to Iranian strategic priorities.

nodes.label: Decoy file / LNK / macro
nodes.notes: The malware branch is an alternative to credential-only operations. Decoy documents and malicious LNK or macro content can establish a workstation foothold.

nodes.label: NICECURL
nodes.notes: Custom APT42 backdoor that downloads modules and supports arbitrary command execution. Uses VBScript and HTTPS. ATT&CK includes T1059.005 and T1071.001.

nodes.label: TAMECAT
nodes.notes: Custom APT42 PowerShell toehold capable of executing PowerShell or C# content. ATT&CK includes T1059.001 and T1071.001.

nodes.label: HTTP(S) command channel
nodes.notes: The backdoors use web protocols for command execution and can serve as a jumping point for additional tooling and collection.

nodes.label: Strategic collection targets
nodes.notes: Targeting follows Iranian intelligence priorities and often concentrates on individuals with access to foreign-policy, defense, political or civil-society information.

nodes.label: Government • diplomacy
nodes.notes: Current and former officials, diplomats, political campaigns and individuals connected to government decision-making are recurring targets.

nodes.label: Think tanks • NGOs • academia
nodes.notes: Researchers, academics, NGOs and policy institutions have been repeatedly targeted through tailored social engineering.

nodes.label: Media • activists • dissidents
nodes.notes: Journalists, activists, political opposition and diaspora communities are relevant to the actor's surveillance and collection mission.

nodes.label: Defense • aerospace
nodes.notes: Defense-linked experts and aerospace personnel have appeared in recent targeting, particularly during periods of regional tension.

nodes.label: UAE / MENA relevance • WATCH
nodes.notes: A commercial actor record includes the UAE among historical target regions. Public 2025 research also reports impersonation of the UAE-based Khaleej Times brand. This supports regional vigilance but does not establish a currently confirmed UAE victim or active UAE infrastructure.

steps.note: APT42 / CALANQUE ION — Iranian cyber espionage focused on information collection and surveillance. The IRGC-IO relationship is a high-confidence assessment; vendor alias scopes are not perfectly identical.
Human-led access: target research, believable personas and extended benign dialogue precede a tailored credential lure delivered by email or messaging services.
Credential path: phishing kits capture passwords and authentication material, enabling valid-account access followed by mailbox and cloud-data collection and export.
Malware path: decoy files can deploy NICECURL or TAMECAT, custom backdoors providing command execution and a web-protocol command channel.

Strategic targeting spans government, diplomacy, think tanks, academia, NGOs, media, activists, dissidents, defense and aerospace. UAE relevance is a watch condition, not proof of a current UAE victim.

Full analytical view: trust-building enables either credential theft and cloud collection or malware-backed access. Keep alias equivalence, UAE relevance and infrastructure attribution evidence-graded.
